name: Samoa
summary_text: Samoa is workable for trans visitors — anchored by one of the world's most institutionalized third-gender traditions. Fa'afafine (and fa'atama) are culturally embedded: recognized as heirs to customary land and eligible for matai (chiefly) titles within fa'a Sāmoa, organized nationally through the Samoa Fa'afafine Association (a formal UN UPR stakeholder since 1987), and visible through a famous pageant culture. Samoa repealed its colonial-era “female impersonation” crime in 2013, so no law touches gender expression itself. The remaining negatives are modest for a visitor: no anti-discrimination law and no legal gender recognition (both resident-facing); documented discrimination, cyberbullying and gender-based violence against fa'afafine (APTN peer-led study — primarily resident/domestic contexts); isolated police-harassment reports (2 respondents, no convictions); and village fono councils that enforce conservative dress and behaviour norms. The unenforced sodomy statute is a situational risk for a fraction of visitors, not a trans-universal one.

sources.title: Reimagining our Future: A Recap of the Asia Pacific Transgender Network Convening in the Pacific Islands – Asia Pacific Transgender Network
sources.claim_summary: APTN (May 2024): recap of the Asia Pacific Transgender Network convening in Nadi, Fiji - brought together gender-diverse community members from across the Pacific (including Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Hawaii, Niue, Papua New Guinea, Tahiti, Tokelau, Tonga) on health and well-being, intersectionality and legal gender recognition.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Samoa's criminalisation of same-sex activity (up to 5 years under the Crimes Act 2013).

Samoa Fa'afafine Association (SFA) stakeholder report for Samoa's UPR (39th session, 2021): 'The Protection of the Rights of Fa'afafine/Fa'atama/LGBTIQ/SOGIESC persons in Samoa' - describes the culturally unique third-gender identities fa'afafine and fa'atama and documents lived experiences and struggles, with the aim of establishing grounds for non-discriminatory policy and legislation.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters feature covers Samoa's third gender (fa'afafine) delicately balancing sex and religion.
NOTE: The APTN Samoa socio-economic study returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

sources.title: Relief among Samoan fa'afafine at removal of impersonation crime | RNZ
sources.claim_summary: RNZ Pacific (May 2013): relief among Samoan fa'afafine at removal of the impersonation crime - under the new Crimes Act the crime of 'impersonating a woman' was scrapped; SFA president To'oto'oali'i Roger Stanley describes the relief (the section had not been enforced for decades but could have been revived); notes the sodomy provision remains and the community is not agitating about it.

Johanna Schmidt, 'Redefining Fa'afafine: Western Discourses and the Construction of Transgenderism in Samoa' (Intersections, Aug 2001): academic analysis of fa'afafine ('in the manner of a woman') - biological males expressing feminine gender identities; argues fa'afafine are both viewed through and influenced by Western understandings of sexuality; Auckland as the largest Pacific city hosts considerable fa'afafine and fakaleiti populations.

UN Free & Equal Pacific information sheet (Aug 2015): FAQ on sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex status in the Pacific - documents the fa'afafine of Samoa (with American Samoa and Tokelau) among the diverse pre-colonial Pacific gender identities that are 'important parts of the cultural treasure of the region'.
